text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx + timeouts on /v1/generate (error_rate=23% 5m, p95 latency=3.2s). Paging @ryan. Incident ID: INC-2026-314. Metrics: https://monitoring.redwood/internal/alerts/INC-2026-314

ryan: acked. I'm on it. First check: are gateway health checks ok?

elena: seeing large queue depth on scheduler-batcher in eu-west-1. head-of-line blocking: many small requests stuck behind a few huge ones. Batcher batch_size stuck at 16 and not draining.

maya: runtime logs show repeated KV cache misses and worker threads in WAIT_FOR_BATCH state. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T10:03:12Z runtime INFO waiting_for_batch id=worker-7 wait_ms=1200
2026-03-15T10:04:01Z runtime WARN kv_cache_miss id=req-9a2f
2026-03-15T10:04:45Z runtime ERROR handler timeout id=req-12b3 status=504
```

raj: confirmed spike concentrated in eu-west-1 (only). us-west unaffected. Could be traffic surge to that region.

alex: customers (big-saas, partner-x) reporting 502/504s in EU. Support notified them we are investigating.

ryan: quick probes: gateway OK (200 on /health). But hitting /v1/generate returns 504 reproducible from eu proxies. Dumping queue depths from scheduler api:
```
$ curl -s http://scheduler.eu-west-1.internal/queues | jq '.batchers[] | {id, queued, active, avg_batch_size}'
{ "id": "batcher-3", "queued": 1247, "active": 48, "avg_batch_size": 16 }
{ "id": "batcher-4", "queued": 1102, "active": 46, "avg_batch_size": 16 }
```

ryan: ok that matches head-of-line. Some requests are huge and block many small requests. Plan: 1) temporarily reduce max_batch_size and async-shed large requests, 2) scale batcher replicas in EU, 3) enable fallback route to lighter model variant to drain.

elena: +1. Changing scheduler config to prefer small requests (batch_by_size=true, max_batch_size=8) should reduce hol. I'll roll a canary config to 25% of traffic. Command I'll run:
```bash
kubectl -n redwood patch configmap scheduler-config -p '{"data":{"max_batch_size":"8","batching_policy":"prefer_small"}}'
```

maya: also recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for frequent prefixes — enabling cache should cut token work for repeated context. I'll flip the cache flag on the model runtime group.

raj: scaling batcher pods now: `kubectl -n redwood scale deployment batcher-eu --replicas=12`

deploy-bot: Deployment "batcher-eu" scaled to 12 replicas by raj at 2026-03-15T10:08:02Z :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: Observability note: adding temporary routing rule to send 30% of EU traffic to fallback-smaller-model (latency tradeoff).

ryan: applying canary config and fallback now. Will monitor error rate.

elena: canary config applied to 25% of batcher-4. avg queue depth on canary nodes dropping to ~300 after scaling.

maya: KV cache flag enabled for model-group-a. cache hit rate now 0 -> 18% within first 2 minutes.

ryan: error_rate down to 7% in the last 2m, p95 down to 1.1s. Gateway 5xx much reduced. Still seeing intermittent 504s on old nodes - will drain them.

raj: draining old batcher pods: `kubectl -n redwood cordon batcher-3 && kubectl -n redwood drain batcher-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

deploy-bot: Pod batcher-3 cordoned and draining initiated by raj.

alex: letting customers know we have mitigations in place and error rates are dropping. ETA to resolution ~15-30m pending drains.

rachel: taking over monitoring for next hour. Ryan handing off active incident. @ryan please include runbook steps in thread so I can take over incident doc.

ryan: handing over. Runbook short notes: 1) reduce max_batch_size to 8 (canary then roll), 2) scale batcher-eu replicas up, 3) enable fallback routing to smaller model, 4) enable KV caching for hot prefixes, 5) drain degraded nodes, 6) watch queue depth and p95. I'll post exact commands in casebook.

rachel: noted. I'll keep watch and escalate if error_rate >= 10% after 20m.

incident-bot: ALERT UPDATE: error_rate=5% (5m), incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Closing page for primary oncall.

ryan: thanks team — will follow up with root cause postmortem. Suspect scheduler batching policy + cache cold start + regional traffic surge.

elena: filing incident ticket INC-2026-314 with initial timeline and actions.

alex: customers updated. Marking customer-impact field: EU users affected, degraded but stable.

rachel: taking final notes and will run a quick follow-up 1:1 with runtime team to harden batching config.
